## Description

Raise the conda `brotli-python` in `docker/base-deps` and
`docker/base-slim` to 1.2.1 to pick up the fix for CVE-2026-111497
("Node2Shell",
[GHSA-9v8h-qqgm-4m35](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-9v8h-qqgm-4m35)):
an out-of-bounds write in the Brotli decoder (upstream fix:
google/brotli@0ed4268). PyPI/conda `Brotli` <= 1.2.0 bundle the
vulnerable decoder; 1.2.1 is the fixed release. The CVE is in CISA KEV.

The Miniforge 24.11.3 installer used by both Dockerfiles ships
`brotli-python 1.1.0` in its base environment, and none of the pip lock
files manage it. So every image built on these bases (`ray`, `ray-ml`,
`ray-llm`) carries the vulnerable decoder, both in `site-packages` and
as a second copy in the conda package cache. `urllib3`, `requests`,
`aiohttp` and `httpx` use Brotli automatically when it is installed.

What changes:

- **Python >= 3.11:** add `brotli-python>=1.2.1` to the existing `conda
install`. The following `conda clean` removes the superseded package
from the cache.
- **Python 3.10:** conda-forge has no py3.10 build of `brotli-python`
1.2.1 (the newest is 1.2.0), so a floor would make the solve fail. For
3.10 the conda package is removed, `Brotli==1.2.1` is installed from
PyPI, and the cache is cleaned again. This branch can go when 3.10 is
deprecated.

Alternative considered: moving to a newer Miniforge installer. Miniforge
26.9.4 does ship `brotli-python 1.2.1`, but its base is Python 3.14 /
conda 26.9.4, and the existing `conda install python=<ver> ...` step
then downgrades conda to 23.9.0 on 3.12 and fails to solve on 3.10. That
is a much larger change than a one-package floor.

None filed. Advisory: GHSA-9v8h-qqgm-4m35 / CVE-2026-111497.

Tested by building both Dockerfiles locally with `docker buildx build`
(ubuntu:22.04, CPU):

| Dockerfile | Python | linux/amd64 | linux/arm64 |
|---|---|---|---|
| base-deps | 3.10, 3.11, 3.12, 3.13, 3.14 | OK | OK |
| base-slim | 3.10, 3.11, 3.12, 3.13, 3.14 | OK | see below |

In every image that built: `Brotli` 1.2.1, a compress/decompress round
trip works, no Brotli < 1.2.1 remains in `site-packages`, the conda
package cache or `conda-meta`, and `libbrotli1` is 1.0.9-2ubuntu0.1
(Ubuntu's fix, picked up by the existing `apt-get upgrade`).

the Ray CI image pipelines (needs the `go` label), and `base-slim` on
linux/arm64, which fails to build on `master` with or without this
change (`psutil==5.9.8` has no aarch64 wheel and the slim image has no

[Data] Restrict PIL image decoding to a safe format allowlist (#67752)

## Summary

`read_images`, the `read_webdataset` default decoder, and the LeRobot
image-camera decoder passed untrusted bytes straight to `PIL.Image.open`
with no format restriction. PIL picks a plugin by **file signature, not
extension**, so a payload named `a.jpg` that actually contains EPS bytes
is routed to PIL's EPS plugin — which shells out to the external
**Ghostscript** binary. On a host with a vulnerable Ghostscript this can
execute code in the Ray worker.

This is the image sibling of the `.pkl`/`.pt` decoder hardening done in
GHSA-hhrp-gw25-jr43; that fix
(https://github.com/ray-project/ray/pull/63469) added a deserialization
guard but did not add an image-format allowlist.

Fix: restrict all three decoders to a raster-format allowlist via
`Image.open(..., formats=[...])`, so disallowed formats (EPS, etc.) are
rejected before any plugin runs. The allowlist lives in one place
(`_internal/datasource/image_utils.py`) so the readers can't drift
apart.

Addresses GHSA-pwm8-8ghq-qw5p.

## Before

- `ray.data.read_images("a.jpg")` where `a.jpg` holds EPS bytes → PIL
selects the EPS plugin → attempts to launch Ghostscript.
- `ray.data.read_webdataset(tar)` with a member `0001.jpg` holding EPS
bytes → same dispatch via the default decoder.
- `ray.data.read_lerobot(...)` with an image-camera parquet cell holding
EPS bytes → same dispatch in `_decode_image_frames`.
- No allowlist: any format PIL can sniff is reachable from untrusted
input.

"BMP", "GIF"]`, in `_internal/datasource/image_utils.py` (aligned with
`ImageDatasource._FILE_EXTENSIONS`).

- LeRobot: uses `_ALLOWED_PIL_FORMATS`. This covers what LeRobot writes

datasets.

[Data] Gate unsafe deserialization in WebDataset default decoder (#63469)

## Description

The default decoder in `read_webdataset` runs `pickle.loads` on
`.pkl/.pickle` files and `torch.load(weights_only=False)` on `.pt/.pth`
files from attacker-controlled TAR archives, enabling arbitrary code
execution with no opt-in. This is the same class of bug as
GHSA-mw35-8rx3-xf9r (patched in 2.55.0 for Parquet), but in a different
code path that was not addressed.

This PR gates the unsafe `.pkl/.pickle` and `.pt/.pth` branches in
`_default_decoder` behind the
`RAY_DATA_WEBDATASET_ALLOW_UNSAFE_DESERIALIZATION=1` environment
variable. The error message points users to the existing `decoder`
parameter on `ray.data.read_webdataset()` as the safe escape hatch for
custom deserialization.

## Related issues

Fixes GHSA-hhrp-gw25-jr43

## Additional information

- Existing tests that rely on `.pt` round-trip encoding/decoding now use
a `monkeypatch.setenv` fixture to opt in
- New tests verify: rejection of all four unsafe extensions by default,
opt-in via env var, and bypass via custom `decoder` callable

[deps] Bump aiohttp to 3.14.4 for CVE-2026-111064, CVE-2026-111066, GHSA-2g87-pp6c-29x5 (#67304)

Closes #67302

## Why

Three high-severity advisories against aiohttp, all fixed in 3.14.4
(verified in the GitHub Advisory Database):

| Advisory | Affected | Fixed | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|
| CVE-2026-111064 / GHSA-5wr8-gcqf-gqf3 | <= 3.14.3 | 3.14.4 | server
lacks an initial request/header timeout |
| CVE-2026-111066 / GHSA-9xw5-w5jj-pvcg | >= 2.0.0, < 3.14.4 | 3.14.4 |
file descriptor exhaustion in multipart requests |
| GHSA-2g87-pp6c-29x5 | <= 3.14.3 | 3.14.4 | multiple instances of
excessive or unbounded memory/CPU use |

Ray runs aiohttp **servers** in two places, so the server-side DoS
issues apply directly:

- the runtime_env agent
(`python/ray/_private/runtime_env/agent/main.py`, `web.Application`),
from the copy vendored into the wheel via
`RUNTIME_ENV_AGENT_PIP_PACKAGES` (`aiohttp==3.14.3`). This is what
#67302 reports; scanners flag its dist-info regardless of site-packages
and it can't be overridden downstream.
- the dashboard, from site-packages: `requirements_compiled.txt` pins
3.14.3, so every image ships it, and the `>= 3.14.1` floor in
`requirements.txt` / `ray[default]` still allows affected versions for
users.

## What

Same shape as #64056:

- `python/setup.py`: bundled `aiohttp==3.14.4`; `ray[default]` floor
`aiohttp >= 3.14.4`.
- `python/requirements.txt`,
`python/requirements/test-requirements.txt`: `aiohttp>=3.14.4`.
- `ci/build/bundled_dependency_versions_test.py`: expects
`aiohttp==3.14.4` (passes locally).
- `python/requirements/security-requirements.txt`: adds
`aiohttp>=3.14.4`, so a future `ci/ci.sh compile_pip_dependencies` /
`compile_pip_dependencies_py314` run (both take this file as an input)
can't resolve an affected aiohttp. aiohttp's `# via` in both compiled
files gains `-r python/requirements/security-requirements.txt`; no lock
changes, since raydepsets only sees the compiled files. Adjacent-line
edits to the same 3-line file are also in #67305 (certifi) and #67301
(virtualenv); whichever merges later needs a trivial rebase.
- `requirements_compiled.txt` / `requirements_compiled_py3.14.txt` and
all raydepsets locks: aiohttp 3.14.4, yarl 1.23.0 → 1.25.1 (aiohttp
3.14.4 requires `yarl>=1.25.1`; yarl's own deps are unchanged). Every
changed lock line is an aiohttp or yarl version/hash line; the size of
the diff is aiohttp 3.14.4 publishing more wheels (e.g. 161 vs 119
hashes in `ray_img_py312.lock`).

Checks:
- `uv pip compile` of both compiled files with only these two pins
changed resolves on py3.11 / py3.14 with no other version moving.
- aiohttp 3.14.4/3.14.5 publish wheels for cp310–cp314 on linux
x86_64/aarch64, macOS arm64/x86_64 and win_amd64.
- The vendored install (`pip install --target ... aiohttp==3.14.4
idna==3.15`) gives aiohttp 3.14.4, yarl 1.25.1, multidict 6.9.1 on
py3.10 and py3.14, and `from aiohttp import web` imports from the
vendored dir.

**Why 3.14.4 and not 3.14.5:** 3.14.5 only adds a WebSocket
control-frame fix and widens its `multidict` cap to `<8`. The vendored
bundle doesn't pin transitive deps, so 3.14.5 would pull multidict 7.1.0
(a new major) into the runtime_env agent; 3.14.4 keeps it on 6.x. Both
satisfy the issue's `>= 3.14.4`.

**Behavior change in 3.14.4:** `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` posts
with more than 1000 fields now get `413` by default (`client_max_fields`
on `web.Application`).

## Not covered

- `python/deplocks/ci/ci_windows_depset.lock` (aiohttp 3.10.11): the
Windows agent driver env is Python 3.8; aiohttp >= 3.11 requires a newer
Python.
- `release/requirements_py310.txt` (aiohttp 3.9.5): release tooling
(`ray_release`), pip-compiled via Bazel; not shipped.
- `release/ray_release/byod/requirements_ml_byod_3.10.txt` (3.13.3): not
referenced by any config.
- `python/deplocks/ray_img/ray_img_py39.lock`: orphaned, no py3.9
depset.
- `releases/2.60.0` also pins 3.14.3; a cherry-pick is a separate
decision.

CVE-2022-24769.7408258f64d007f24daad7da0d568ec87f87d959:
[core][sandbox] Make Ray Sandbox run Docker-built images out of the box (#65570)

## Description

`ray.experimental.sandbox` cannot run standard Docker-built images
without reaching for the private `_oci_spec_transform_fn` hook and
client-side workarounds. We hit all of these while integrating Ray
Sandbox with the [Harbor](https://github.com/harbor-framework/harbor)
eval framework (see the workarounds carried in
harbor-framework/harbor#2725), and the follow-up items while testing
this PR end-to-end on a live Ray cluster with real gVisor.

### Capabilities

- **`SandboxConfig.capabilities`** (plumbed through `create()`, the
`Sandbox` actor, `SandboxRuntime.create`, and the gVisor backend): None
keeps the runtime default; otherwise the bounding/effective/permitted
sets are written exactly, so `[]` runs with no capabilities at all
(inheritable and ambient untouched, matching modern Docker, which
stopped setting inheritable for CVE-2022-24769). A new
`DOCKER_DEFAULT_CAPABILITIES` constant ([Docker's documented default
set](https://docs.docker.com/engine/containers/run/#runtime-privilege-and-linux-capabilities))
gives Docker parity in one line: the runtime's default (whatever `runsc
spec` emits) grants only three capabilities, and standard images break
confusingly without more — `apt-get` needs `CAP_SETUID`/`CAP_SETGID` for
its `_apt` sub-processes, `tar` extracting as root fatally fails
restoring archived uid/gids (e.g. `1000`) without `CAP_CHOWN`.

### Networking and DNS

- **`network="public"`** — the recommended internet-access mode: host
egress (`--network=host` under the hood) with a **synthetic
`/etc/resolv.conf`** generated from `dns` (default `8.8.8.8`,
`1.1.1.1`). Nothing about the host resolver is inherited, so the config
stays portable and doesn't leak host search domains or internal resolver
addresses (a cluster node's resolv.conf typically carries internal
Kubernetes search domains, the cluster DNS VIP, and `ndots:5`).
- **`network="host"`** stays the explicit power mode — full host network
identity (including internal networks reachable from the node) with the
host's own resolv.conf mounted read-only; `dns=` overrides it with a
generated file. Keeping the modes separate lets the docs state that
difference plainly. `"none"` remains the default.
- **`dns=`** mirrors `docker --dns` and is the escape hatch for
locked-down VPCs that block public DNS; it's rejected for modes that
mount no resolv.conf. Host-side networking also drops the spec's empty
network namespace, which previously left the sandbox loopback-only
despite `--network=host`.
- **`network="sandbox"` with `rootless=True` is rejected at config
time**: runsc refuses the combination at container start, after the
image pull, with an error naming a flag the user never set.

### Working directory and writability

- **Writability is now fully explicit** — determined by the two
parameters the user actually set, with the image's `WORKDIR` inherited
for the *process cwd only*:

  | `readonly` | `workdir` | writable | cwd |
  |---|---|---|---|
| `True` *(default)* | `None` *(default)* | nothing on the rootfs (safe
default; standard tmpfs mounts like `/tmp` remain writable) | image
`WORKDIR`, else `/` |
  | `True` | `/data` | only `/data` (host-backed scratch) | `/data` |
| `False` | any | everything (per-sandbox overlay; image content stays
visible, nothing shadowed) | explicit workdir, else image `WORKDIR` |

Previously the backend defaulted `workdir` to the image's `WORKDIR` (or
`/`) and scratch-mounted there, so what was writable depended on image
metadata invisible in the config. An inherited `WORKDIR` is never
silently made writable now. This made the interim `mount_workdir` knob
redundant, so it's removed; the backend also no longer mutates
`config.workdir` (the resolved cwd lives in sandbox metadata), and
inherited image `WORKDIR` values are no longer used in host path joins,
removing that traversal surface.

### TTL

- **`ttl_seconds` now defaults to `None`** (no TTL) everywhere: the old
1h default was wall-clock from creation, not idle time, so
actively-running sandboxes were deleted mid-work — a silent,
hard-to-attribute failure in long agent runs. Opt-in destruction is the
safer default.
- **`SandboxRuntime` now actually enforces a set TTL** (daemon timer,
canceled on delete); previously the parameter was a documented no-op
below the actor layer, and the `Sandbox` actor's duplicate timer is
dropped in favor of the runtime's.

### Shell for string commands

- String commands ran under `/bin/sh` — `dash` on Debian-family images —
while agent-generated commands overwhelmingly assume bash, failing
confusingly on `[[ ]]`/`pipefail`/arrays. **`SandboxConfig.shell`** now
defaults to `"/bin/bash"` outright (no auto-detection — deterministic
per review), with a per-command `shell=` override on `exec()`. Images
without bash set `shell="/bin/sh"` explicitly, as the busybox-based
tests now do; list commands still bypass the shell.

### Robustness

- `SandboxRuntime.create()` forwards `mount_workdir` into the config (it
was silently dropped — caught by live testing; a new runtime-layer test
suite pins config fields actually reaching the backend, the gap that let
it ship green).
- Caller-supplied `base_spec`s with null capability sets or non-dict
namespace entries no longer raise; malformed namespace entries are kept
for runsc to reject with its own error.
- `SandboxConfig` validates the network mode against `("none", "public",
"host", "sandbox")`.

Defaults are behavior-preserving except where called out (TTL, and
mount_workdir under `readonly=False`); the API is alpha.

## Related issues

Related to #64964 (Ray Sandboxing with gVisor). Enables removing the
OCI-spec transform, DNS seeding, and `tar --no-same-owner` workarounds
in harbor-framework/harbor#2725 / harbor-framework/harbor#2785.

## Additional information

Usage:

```python
from ray.experimental import sandbox
from ray.experimental.sandbox import DOCKER_DEFAULT_CAPABILITIES

sb = sandbox.create(
    image="ubuntu:24.04",
    network="public",
    capabilities=DOCKER_DEFAULT_CAPABILITIES,
    readonly=False,
)
# apt-get / tar / DNS / bash / image WORKDIR all behave as under Docker,
# without inheriting the host's resolver configuration.
```

Testing:
- Unit tests run without runsc or a cluster: spec construction against
`base_spec` with a stub image manager, config validation, resolv.conf
generation policy at the `prepare_oci_bundle` layer, and a new
`SandboxRuntime`-layer suite (fake backend) covering field forwarding
and TTL enforcement.
- Full `TEST_SANDBOX=1` suite with real gVisor/runsc on Linux: 64 tests
pass, including the shell-detection and rootless-rejection paths.
- Docs: new "Networking and DNS" section with the mode table and
security property of each mode, the recommended internet-access example,
the `dns=` escape hatch, and an updated OCI-transform section (its
example used the now-rejected `network="sandbox"` default combination
and hand-mounted resolv.conf).

This is the first of two changes for running Harbor evals on Ray
Sandbox; a follow-up adds an HTTP API service so sandboxes can be
consumed as a standalone service.

[Java] Bump jackson-databind 2.18.6 -> 2.18.8 to fix CVE-2026-54512 and CVE-2026-54513 (#64575)

## Description

Bumps the bundled `jackson-databind` dependency from **2.18.6** to
**2.18.8** in `java/dependencies.bzl`.

`jackson-databind` is shaded into `ray_dist.jar` (relocated to
`io.ray.shaded.com.fasterxml.jackson.*`). Version 2.18.6 is flagged by
security scanners (Sonatype, Salesforce 3PP, etc.) for two
`PolymorphicTypeValidator` (PTV) bypass vulnerabilities, both fixed in
**2.18.8**:

- **CVE-2026-54512** (CVSS 8.1 HIGH): when a type id contains generic
parameters, `DatabindContext._resolveAndValidateGeneric()` validates
only the raw container class and never the nested type arguments, so a
denied class can be smuggled as a generic parameter of an allowed
container (e.g. `java.util.ArrayList<com.evil.Gadget>`), bypassing an
explicitly configured PTV allow-list.
- **CVE-2026-54513** (CVSS 8.1 HIGH): `allowIfSubTypeIsArray()`
allowlists array types based only on `clazz.isArray()` without checking
the element type, so `EvilType[]` is permitted even when `EvilType` is
not allowlisted.

Both CVEs affect `2.10.0` up to (excluding) `2.18.8` and are fixed in
`2.18.8`. This is a patch bump within the 2.18.x line (binary
compatible); `jackson-core` and `jackson-annotations` resolve
transitively to the matching 2.18.8 version.

## Related issues

Related to #64571 (that issue references CVE-2026-54512; this PR also
addresses the closely-related CVE-2026-54513, fixed by the same 2.18.8
release).

- Single-line change to the pinned coordinate in
`java/dependencies.bzl`; there is no `maven_install.json` lockfile to

GHSA-MW35-8RX3-XF9R.8ea9ede2cae27dee755264df922deb1e256db2e3:
[Data] Block pickle object columns when reading untrusted Parquet files (#63470)

## Description

`ArrowPythonObjectScalar.as_py()` calls `pickle.load` on column data
from Parquet files with `ray.data.arrow_pickled_object` columns. Since
this extension type is globally registered on import, any
`ray.data.read_parquet()` call on an attacker-supplied Parquet file
followed by data iteration achieves arbitrary code execution. This is a
variant of GHSA-mw35-8rx3-xf9r (patched in 2.55.0 for tensor metadata)
but through a different sink path.

The guard is placed on the **Parquet read boundary** — not on `as_py()`
itself — because `ArrowPythonObjectType` is used pervasively in Ray
Data's internal pipeline (`from_items`, `map`, shuffles) where the data
is self-produced and trusted. The `pickle.load` in `as_py()` only fires
during row materialization, not during the Parquet read itself, so
checking each table's schema before yielding it is sufficient to prevent
the exploit.

Both V1 (`read_fragments`) and V2
(`ParquetFileReader._iter_fragment_tables`) read paths are guarded,
gated behind `RAY_DATA_AUTOLOAD_PICKLE_OBJECT_SCALAR=1`. V1 checks the
env var on the driver in `ParquetDatasource.__init__` and propagates the
flag to workers via the read task closure. V2 checks it in
`ParquetFileReader.__init__` (also driver-side) and carries it via
pickling.

## Related issues

Fixes DATA-2364 (GHSA-2g92-c6pv-7g2q)

## Additional information

- `as_py()` is unchanged — internal paths (`from_items`, `map`, etc.)
are unaffected
- Tests use `runtime_env` to propagate the env var to workers,
parametrized over V1 and V2
- Rejection test uses an `Exploit` class with `__reduce__` and asserts
the marker file is never created

[Data] Gate unsafe deserialization in WebDataset default decoder (#63469)

## Description

The default decoder in `read_webdataset` runs `pickle.loads` on
`.pkl/.pickle` files and `torch.load(weights_only=False)` on `.pt/.pth`
files from attacker-controlled TAR archives, enabling arbitrary code
execution with no opt-in. This is the same class of bug as
GHSA-mw35-8rx3-xf9r (patched in 2.55.0 for Parquet), but in a different
code path that was not addressed.

This PR gates the unsafe `.pkl/.pickle` and `.pt/.pth` branches in
`_default_decoder` behind the
`RAY_DATA_WEBDATASET_ALLOW_UNSAFE_DESERIALIZATION=1` environment
variable. The error message points users to the existing `decoder`
parameter on `ray.data.read_webdataset()` as the safe escape hatch for
custom deserialization.

Fixes GHSA-hhrp-gw25-jr43

- Existing tests that rely on `.pt` round-trip encoding/decoding now use
a `monkeypatch.setenv` fixture to opt in
- New tests verify: rejection of all four unsafe extensions by default,
opt-in via env var, and bypass via custom `decoder` callable
